az_heart_cave_and_surroundings.blurb: Heart Cave is the first cluster of problems you reach in Gloria's, a bouldering zone on the lower slopes of Mount Elden above Flagstaff, at roughly 7,000 feet. The dacite is hard on skin, and the lines are thin and technical. Around 16 problems sit in and around a shallow cave and the boulder just to its left, ranging from V0 to double-digit, with the bulk falling between V3 and V7. Expect tall lines with a drop-off feel, so bring several pads and a spotter. Pine forest surrounds the boulders and the walk from the road end is short, making it an easy after-work session.
az_heart_cave_and_surroundings.approach: A well-worn trail leads from the end of the Paradise Rd. cul-de-sac up to the cave; it takes about 5 minutes.

az_pharaoh.blurb: Pharaoh is a small wall in the Bear Canyon sector of Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalina Mountains outside Tucson, at around 7,000 feet. It is mostly a trad crag, with a few bolted lines mixed in. Of the 16 routes, grades span from 5.7 to the low 5.12s, and most are 5.10 or easier. Several are multi-pitch. The wall faces east and stays warm on cool days, though wind can pick up higher on the face. Its elevation makes it a pleasant escape when the desert floor is hot.

az_3_spine_cave.blurb: Spine Cave is a shallow, blocky limestone cave in Dry Canyon in southern Arizona. All 15 routes are bolted sport lines, running from the upper 5.10s through the 5.12s and into the low 5.13s, with the largest group in the 5.11 to 5.12 range. A handful of longer moderates make good warm-ups before the harder, steeper lines. The stone is featured and friendly on the hands, with slopey ledges, incuts, gastons and a distinctive tufa in the middle of the cave. This is a destination for climbers who already lead 5.11 and up.

az_east_side_2.blurb: East Side is a granite wall of up to about 80 feet in the Granite Dells near Prescott, part of the Miyazaki cluster of rounded boulders above Boulder Creek. Nearly all of the 15 routes are trad, with a single bolted line, and most are bunched in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, with a few easier lines at 5.8 and 5.9 and some stiffer 5.12s. The routes are steep and can be top-roped from anchors above, so a rigging rope is handy. The wall collects good winter sun.

az_delta_dome.blurb: Delta Dome is a granite crag high on Mount Lemmon in the Santa Catalinas near Tucson, at about 7,250 feet, set across the canyon from The Steep above Sabino Creek. Most of its 15 routes are bolted, with two trad lines, and the grades run from 5.9 to 5.12, centered on 5.11. Climbing ranges from knobby face moves to pumpy steep sections on the big fin and airy arêtes. Because walls face a mix of directions, you can usually find sun or shade, and the fin blocks some wind. It is quieter than many of the mountain's busier walls.
az_delta_dome.approach: Take the Aspen Trail south, then follow the old firebreak east before turning south along cairns that run parallel to Sabino Creek.

az_peter_pan_playground.blurb: Peter Pan Playground is a roadside cluster of boulders in Euro Dog Valley, part of Queen Creek Canyon near Superior in central Arizona, at about 3,900 feet. It holds 15 boulder problems on welded tuff, a few with an optional one-bolt top rope. The spread is wide: a good group of easy lines from V0 to V2, a middle band to about V5, and a pair of very hard V12 projects. Most problems face west or north, so mornings are warmer and afternoons cooler. The boulders are close together and the walk in is brief.
